sources.entry: OpenNaga - Open-source Razer Synapse alternative for the Naga V2 HyperSpeed that remaps the side buttons and sets DPI and polling rate. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Zer0codestuff/OpenNaga) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: OpenNaga is a free, open-source macOS app that replaces Razer Synapse for the Razer Naga V2 HyperSpeed, handling side-button remapping, onboard profile saving, DPI and polling rate.
summary.what_it_does: It remaps the 12 side buttons and extra mouse controls to keyboard keys, shortcuts, key sequences, mouse actions, app launches, shell commands, macros, or profile switches, with a Hypershift second layer. Profiles can be saved into the mouse's onboard memory so they work without the app, including over Bluetooth, and imported back from the mouse. It reads and changes DPI and polling rate (125/500/1000 Hz) over the USB receiver via the Razer USB protocol. App profiles switch the live assignments automatically when a Dock app comes to the front, done in software. It also provides 25 system actions (audio, playback, brightness, screenshots, windows/spaces, macOS tools) and separate scroll sensitivity sliders.
use_cases: remap Razer Naga V2 HyperSpeed side buttons on Mac
save button profile to mouse memory
set DPI and polling rate on a Mac
map mouse buttons to macOS shortcuts and screenshots
how_to_run: Download OpenNaga-v2.7.0.dmg from the latest release, or build from source
Drag OpenNaga.app to Applications and do not move it afterwards
Right-click the app and choose Open on first launch (release is not notarized)
Grant Accessibility and Input Monitoring permissions when prompted
Open the settings window from the menu bar icon, turn on Remapping, and assign actions
From source: bash Scripts/build_app.sh, then open OpenNaga.app
notable: Saves a profile into the mouse's onboard memory so it keeps working without the app and over Bluetooth
Per-app profile switching in software, works over Bluetooth
Re-sends mouse keys with keyboard modifiers held, since macOS does not combine modifiers across devices
Hypershift layer that can also be stored in mouse memory
Forked from NagaController by DParent10; MIT licensed
caveats: Requires macOS 13.0 or later; the DMG is Apple Silicon only, Intel Macs must build from source
Release is not notarized; DPI, polling and onboard saving need the USB HyperSpeed receiver, and Accessibility and Input Monitoring permissions are required
